title: Can AI tools assess coding assignments?
summary: Researchers from Nature examine whether AI grading tools can fairly evaluate student coding work, raising questions about bias, accuracy, and the future of automated assessment in education.

title: AI tools extract hidden health insights from routine chest imaging
summary: New AI models trained on standard chest X-rays are surfacing predictive health signals such as cardiovascular risk markers that radiologists often overlook, opening a new frontier in preventive diagnostics.

title: As AI reshapes development research, investing in data must be a key priority
summary: IFPRI analysts argue that without high-quality, well-governed data infrastructure, AI potential to accelerate global development research will remain unrealized, calling for sustained investment from funders and governments.

title: Anthropic, Gates Foundation Launch $200 Million AI Partnership
summary: Anthropic and the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation announced a $200 million collaboration aimed at deploying Claude-powered AI tools in global health, agriculture, and poverty-reduction programs across developing nations.

title: First Coders, Now Lawyers? Anthropic Unveils Claude New Legal AI Tools
summary: Anthropic has launched specialized legal reasoning capabilities in Claude, enabling law firms to use the AI for contract review, case research, and compliance analysis, extending its reach well beyond software development.

title: AI could put people off tech jobs and hurt the economy, warns Raspberry Pi boss
summary: The CEO of Raspberry Pi cautioned that widespread AI adoption may discourage young people from pursuing technical careers, creating a long-term skills shortage that paradoxically undermines the very industry AI is meant to accelerate.

title: Employers adopt AI tools faster than they can train workers to use them
summary: HR Dive reports that many organizations are rolling out AI productivity tools across departments before adequate training programs exist, leaving employees overwhelmed and reducing the tools potential return on investment.

title: The growth of build-your-own legal AI tools
summary: The Financial Times explores how large law firms and corporate legal departments are moving beyond off-the-shelf AI products, building proprietary tools on foundation models to better fit their specific workflows and confidentiality requirements.
